\hypertarget{doc-api-vs-cli}{%
\chapter{Akeyless REST API or CLI?}\label{doc-api-vs-cli}}

\hypertarget{short-answer}{%
\section{Short answer}\label{short-answer}}

They are two clients of \textbf{the same operations}. Neither one can read or export configuration that
the other can\textquotesingle t. Choose by where the command runs and how it authenticates, not by what it can reach.

\hypertarget{evidence}{%
\section{Evidence}\label{evidence}}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The Akeyless OpenAPI specification (Go SDK v5.0.x) has 666 operations, 665 of them \texttt{POST}.
  659 of their request schemas are declared in Akeyless\textquotesingle s Go package \texttt{go/src/client/commands},
  which holds the CLI command definitions. The REST API and the CLI flags come from the same
  structs, so a CLI flag is the API field in kebab-case (\texttt{-\/-role-name} = \texttt{role-name}).
\item
  \texttt{akeyless\ \textless{}command\textgreater{}\ -\/-json} prints the response document of the matching API operation. This
  repository proves the equivalence: the exporter reads the same fixture account through the
  CLI, through REST and from saved JSON, and a test requires byte-identical output
  (\texttt{test\_transports\_produce\_identical\_output}).
\item
  The Terraform provider uses the REST API (Go SDK). Anything Terraform reads, the API returns.
\end{itemize}

\hypertarget{differences-that-do-matter}{%
\section{Differences that do matter}\label{differences-that-do-matter}}

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\columnwidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2100}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\columnwidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3950}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\columnwidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3750}}@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
CLI
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
REST API
\end{minipage} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
Authentication & profiles in \texttt{\textasciitilde{}/.akeyless/profiles}, interactive SAML/OIDC browser login (\texttt{akeyless\ configure}) & send \texttt{token} in every JSON body; get one from \texttt{POST\ /auth} (any access type, e.g. \texttt{jwt} in CI) \\
Installation & binary (S3 download or brew) that runners must be allowed to fetch & HTTPS to \texttt{api.akeyless.io} or your Gateway only \\
Command names & \texttt{folder\ get}, \texttt{list-groups}, \texttt{auth-method\ create\ oidc}, \texttt{policy\ list} & \texttt{/folder-get}, \texttt{/list-group}, \texttt{/auth-method-create-oidc}, \texttt{/policy-list} \\
Gateway operations & \texttt{-\/-gateway-url\ https://\textless{}gw\textgreater{}:8000} on each command & base URL \texttt{https://\textless{}gw\textgreater{}:8000/api/v2} \\
Client-side helpers & \texttt{set-role-rule\ -\/-file-rules} (bulk JSON; the API takes one rule per call), \texttt{-\/-jq-expression}, \texttt{connect} (SRA sessions), \texttt{agent}, \texttt{mcp}, \texttt{update} & none \\
Output & JSON with \texttt{-\/-json}, text otherwise & always JSON \\
\end{longtable}

\texttt{/configure} and \texttt{/connect} also appear in the specification, because it\textquotesingle s generated from the CLI
commands. They\textquotesingle re client workflows (profiles, SSH/RDP sessions): don\textquotesingle t build on them over REST (VERIFY).

\hypertarget{decision-rules}{%
\section{Decision rules}\label{decision-rules}}

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\columnwidth - 2\tabcolsep) * \real{0.5371}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\columnwidth - 2\tabcolsep) * \real{0.4429}}@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Situation
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Use
\end{minipage} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
Any persistent change (roles, auth methods, folders, issuers, settings...) & \textbf{Terraform} (REST via the provider), through the pipeline \\
A person exploring or exporting with their SSO login & \textbf{CLI} (\texttt{watchover\ export\ -\/-transport\ cli\ -\/-profile\ \textless{}sso-profile\textgreater{}}) \\
CI jobs: exports, drift reports, verification without the CLI binary & \textbf{REST} (\texttt{watchover\ token} -\textgreater{} \texttt{watchover\ export\ -\/-transport\ api}) \\
Locked-down runners that can\textquotesingle t download binaries & \textbf{REST} \\
Secure Remote Access sessions, the local agent, MCP & \textbf{CLI} (client-side features) \\
One-off bulk rule changes during an incident & CLI \texttt{set-role-rule\ -\/-file-rules}, then codify in Git \\
An operation documented only in the API reference & \textbf{REST} (the CLI usually has it under a similar name: check \texttt{-h}) \\
\end{longtable}

\hypertarget{did-the-cli-unlock-more-exports}{%
\section{Did the CLI unlock more exports?}\label{did-the-cli-unlock-more-exports}}

Not by itself: the reads are the same. Going through the full list of read operations
(76 \texttt{list-*}, \texttt{get-*} and \texttt{describe-*} calls) did show families the exporter wasn\textquotesingle t using yet.
They\textquotesingle re now exported with \texttt{-\/-hcl}:

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\columnwidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.1050}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\columnwidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2700}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\columnwidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.6050}}@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Family
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Read operation
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Terraform resources
\end{minipage} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
Targets & \texttt{list-targets} & \texttt{akeyless\_target\_*} (aws, azure, gcp, k8s and hashi\_vault confirmed from the provider\textquotesingle s constants; other types matched by name and marked VERIFY) \\
Groups (OIDC apps) & \texttt{list-groups} / \texttt{/list-group} & \texttt{akeyless\_group} \\
Gateway & \texttt{gateway-get-config} & \texttt{akeyless\_gateway\_defaults}, \texttt{\_cache}, \texttt{\_remote\_access}, \texttt{\_log\_forwarding\_\textless{}type\textgreater{}}, \texttt{\_migration\_\textless{}type\textgreater{}}, \texttt{\_allowed\_access} \\
\end{longtable}

Still not exportable through either client:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Event forwarders: \texttt{get-event-forwarder} reads one by name, and there is no list.
\item
  Rotated and dynamic secret definitions: \texttt{rotated-secret-list} and \texttt{dynamic-secret-list} exist,
  but their producer types aren\textquotesingle t yet mapped to provider resources.
\item
  Secret values: excluded on purpose.
\end{itemize}

For ad-hoc SQL inventory queries outside Terraform, the community also publishes a Steampipe plugin
(\texttt{akeyless-community/akeyless}, tables such as \texttt{akeyless\_target} and \texttt{akeyless\_gateway}).

\hypertarget{in-this-kit}{%
\section{In this kit}\label{in-this-kit}}

\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\footnotesize,breaklines,breakanywhere,frame=leftline,framerule=1.2pt,rulecolor=\color{wo-rule},xleftmargin=6pt]
## person with an SSO CLI profile
scripts/watchover export --out export/ --transport cli --profile my-sso
## CI, no CLI binary
export AKEYLESS_TOKEN=$(CI_JWT=$JWT AKEYLESS_ACCESS_ID=p-xxxx scripts/watchover token)
scripts/watchover export --out export/ --transport api --hcl --types targets,groups,gateway \
  --gateway-api https://gw.example.com:8000/api/v2
\end{Verbatim}
